evals.prompt: Add a search tool to my TypeScript MCP server. The description can be short; the model will inspect the schema. Show the Zod input and output schemas and the error shape. No tools are available; answer in prose.
evals.expected_output: Requires a what + when description, a typed input schema, a return schema, and actionable errors; the description is how the model selects the tool.
expectations: Requires a description that states what the tool does and when to use it
Requires typed input and return schemas

evals.prompt: Our REST API has 7 endpoints (list, get, create, update, delete, search, export). Expose every endpoint as its own MCP tool. Seven tools is fine if it covers everything. No tools are available; answer in prose.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on endpoint-per-tool sprawl, proposes a small set of workflow tools, and explains the context cost of tool definitions.
expectations: Does not map every endpoint to a tool by default
Proposes workflow-level tools or a smaller surface
Explains that tool definitions consume context on every request

evals.prompt: I ran `python server.py` to test my stdio MCP server and my terminal is stuck. No tools are available. What should I do differently, and what is the minimum real test?
evals.expected_output: Explains that an MCP server is long-running and should be exercised through the evaluation harness, a tmux session, or a timeout, not run directly in the main shell.
expectations: Identifies the hang as expected for a long-running server
Recommends the evaluation harness or a timeout/tmux
Requires an initialize plus real tool call as the test
